title: fix: keep weekly evals running past model rate limits
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #16247

- Pace questions for models that advertise `per_user_rpm`, including the one-request-per-minute community model that stopped the full run.
- Mark a model unscored if it still exhausts 429 retries; publish other scores and show that state separately from budget skips.
- Keep key, balance, permission, and missing-usage failures fatal.

Checks: 21 focused tests pass; Biome and `git diff --check` pass. The local Model Monitor build could not start because this worktree lacks `tsup`.

gist.headline: One slow model, no pileup
gist.blurb: Weekly evals learn to wait for models with tight rate limits. If one still runs out of 429 retries, the other scores carry on.
gist.summary: Weekly evals pace questions using each model's advertised per_user_rpm, including one-request-per-minute models, and mark models that exhaust 429 retries as unscored while publishing the other scores.
gist.impact: Model Monitor can show the remaining weekly scores and distinguish a rate-limited, unscored model from one skipped for budget; key, balance, permission, and missing-usage failures remain fatal.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy evaluation garden with a clock beside a slow-growing code-plant marked '1/min'; Polli, wearing a tiny stopwatch, tends it while a friendly CRT robot carries completed scorecards past a separate unscored card. The scene represents paced questions and a weekly run that continues when one model hits its retry limit.
